name: Illumina
description: Illumina makes DNA-sequencing machines and, mostly, the consumables that run in them: flow cells, reagents and library-prep kits. Consumables were $3.23 billion of $4.34 billion revenue in 2025 (74%) versus only $482 million of instrument sales, so the installed base of sequencers is what it really monetises, each run consuming its chips. Customers are genomic research centers, academic and government labs, hospitals, pharma and biotech, clinical molecular labs and consumer genomics firms. It reports one segment (Core Illumina) after spinning off cancer-screening company GRAIL on 2024-06-24. China is a drag: regulators put Illumina on the unreliable entities list on 2025-02-04, and Greater China revenue fell from $384M (2023) to $243M (2025). In January 2026 it bought proteomics company SomaLogic.

employees.note: About 8,600 full-time plus 50 part-time employees, plus 1,430 contingent workers; about 4,740 in the Americas, 1,280 in Europe.

businessLines.name: Sequencing
businessLines.how: Sells sequencers (NovaSeq, etc.) one-time and then the flow cells, reagents and library-prep kits consumed in every run (consumables $2,939M of sequencing revenue vs instruments $465M), plus sequencing services and support contracts.

businessLines.name: Microarray
businessLines.how: Sells SNP genotyping and gene-expression array chips and kits (mostly consumables, $288M) used in population genetics and consumer genomics, plus services.

brands.name: NovaSeq, Illumina Connected Multiomics
brands.note: Product families; consumables for the NovaSeq X platform drive consumables growth; no brand revenue breakdown.

brands.name: SomaLogic (acquired from Standard BioTools)
brands.note: Acquired 2026-01-30 for total purchase price $460M ($382M cash plus $81M contingent consideration); up to $75M further milestone payments and a 2% royalty to Standard BioTools; proteomics (protein measurement) business. Revenue not read.
